summary: The audit checks the 60 units: CSRE 100, one CSRE 101 comparative core course, one Major Core course (JEWISHST 77, 115 or 117), a methodology course (3-5 units), a community-engaged learning course or experience, CSRE 200X or 201X as WIM and capstone, and electives from JEWISHST courses, up to 8 units of AFRICAAM, ASNAMST, CHILATST, CSRE or NATIVEAM courses and up to 15 units of Hebrew or Yiddish. Courses must be letter graded unless offered S/NC only, and core, methodology, WIM and capstone courses need a C- or better. Checked by hand: petitioned courses (up to 15 units), other languages such as Ladino, external credit (up to 20 units), no more than two S/NC classes, a CEL experience without a course, and honors.

PYNSqLu6.why: "Jewish Studies majors must complete the remaining units of their 60-unit minimum with elective coursework in Jewish Studies." "Jewish Studies majors may count up to 8 units of Department of African and African American Studies (DAAAS), Asian American Studies (ASNAMST), Chicana/o-Latina/o Studies (CHILATST), Comparative Studies in Race and Ethnicity (CSRE), or Native American Studies (NATIVEAM) courses toward their degree" (DAAAS courses are AFRICAAM). "Jewish Studies majors may count up to 15 units of language study"; "Languages counted toward the major include Hebrew, Yiddish, Ladino, and other approved languages". Policies: "No more than 15 units of petitioned courses that are not listed under CCSRE or cross-listed with CCSRE may be applied to electives"; those, other languages and external credit (up to 20 units) are moved in by hand. The WIM, capstone and honors courses (CSRE 200X, 201X-Z) count where they are required, not against the 8 units. The 15 language units are a program cap, because Hebrew courses are cross-listed in JEWISHST and would otherwise count as Jewish Studies electives.
